::: {#exm-reed-solomon}
#### A small Reed--Solomon code

Take $q = n = 5$, $k = 2$, and the points $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ of $\ffield{5}$,
the integers modulo 5.
The message $m = (1, 2)$ gives the line $f_m(t) = 1 + 2t$, and

$$E(m) = (1, 3, 0, 2, 4),$$

since $f_m(2) = 5 \equiv 0$, $f_m(3) = 7 \equiv 2$ and $f_m(4) = 9 \equiv 4$.
By @thm-reed-solomon-distance the minimum distance is $5 - 2 + 1 = 4$,
so the code corrects one error.
In terms of lines: with one error, the true line passes through
at least four of the five received values.
Any other line meets the true line in at most one point,
so it passes through at most two of the received values,
and the nearest codeword is the true line.

:::
